# HarnMem
**Cross-harness agent memory that lives in plain files.**

> HarnMem = *harness* + *memory* (`harn` is also a Scots word for "brains").
> One user, one machine
, one memory store — shared by every coding agent you use.

HarnMem is a portable memory system for coding agents. It stores memories as
plain Markdown files un

der `~/.harnmem/`, retrieves them with a local
deterministic engine, and injects a small, byte-stabl

e hot index into each
harness session. The same store is readable by every adapter and by the CLI, s

o
a memory written in one harness is available in another — no server, no vector
database, no embedd
ing model, and no runtime dependencies in the engine.

- **Packages:** `@harnmem/core` (engine), `@harnmem/cli` (`harnmem` command),
`pi-harnmem` (pi exten

sion, listed in the
pi.dev package gallery), `dsh-harnmem`
(DSH plugin), `claude-harnmem`
(Claude Co

de plugin), `codex-harnmem` (Codex CLI plugin),
`opencode-harnmem` (opencode v2 plugin), `grok-harnm

em` (Grok CLI plugin),
`cursor-harnmem` (Cursor desktop plugin), `hermes-harnmem` (Hermes Agent
memo

ry provider, installed through Hermes' own plugin manager) and
`omp-harnmem` (oh-my-pi extension plu

gin) — all published
on npm except `hermes-harnmem`, which installs through Hermes' own plugin
manag

er (above). Install the CLI with
`npm install -g @harnmem/cli`; the opencode adapter needs
opencode

2.x and is verified end to end on the 2.1.4 binary (injection, native
tools, per-turn journaling); t

he Grok adapter is verified on the 1.0.70 binary
(MCP `initialize.instructions` injection, six tools

, session-end extraction);
the Cursor adapter is verified on Cursor 3.27.22 (first-prompt injection,

plugin MCP tools, session-end journaling); the Hermes adapter is verified on

## Why another memory plugin?
| Approach | Limitation for this use case |
| mem0 / Zep / Letta / OpenViking | Requires a service, vector database or Docker; heavy to install

and operate |
| pi-memory | Effective inside pi, but not shared with other harnesses and no lifecycl

e governance |
| dsh-auto-memory | DSH-only; cross-session but not cross-harness |
| Built-in harnes

s memory (e.g. ZCode) | Tied to one harness; store layout not reusable |
| Just put everything in `A
GENTS.md` | No retrieval, no governance; grows noisy until models ignore it |

HarnMem's bet: **the source of truth is the file system, retrieval happens in
the local process, and
lifecycle decisions are explainable and reversible.**
## Features

- **Cross-harness by construction.** The store and data model are
harness-agnostic; adapters are thi

n. The same store is shared by the pi,
DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Grok, Cursor,

Hermes and omp
adapters and by the CLI
without any harness.
- **File-native SSOT.** One memory per

Markdown file with YAML frontmatter.
Indexes and digests are derived and rebuildable; a corrupt inde

x costs a
rebuild, never data.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** `@harnmem/core` and `@harnmem/cli` u

se only
Node.js built-ins. No native modules, no downloads, no background daemon.
- **Precise recall

without embeddings.** CJK-aware tokenization (character
bigrams), BM25F field weighting, entity/tag

/time filters, two-hop link
diffusion, and an explainable score blending lexical relevance with
impo

rtance, confidence, recency, usage, pins, links and staleness.
- **Memory that ages well.** ADD-only

writes with bi-temporal supersede keep
history; mechanical dedupe/merge keeps the store small; valu

e-based retention
moves entries active -> archived -> trashed; `trash/` + restore and an
append-only

`state/audit.jsonl` keep it auditable.
- **KV-cache-friendly injection.** The injected block is reb

uilt only on session
start, compaction, memory writes and day rollover, and is byte-identical
betwee

n turns, so prompt caches keep hitting.
- **A vocabulary that grows with your corpus.** The shipped

synonym tables are
generic on purpose; `harnmem synonyms suggest` reads your own memories, asks a
mo

del for interchangeable terms a co-occurrence pass could never find (Chinese
jargon usually shares n

o characters), validates every group against the corpus,
and writes reviewed proposals to a local `-

suggested` table. `synonyms check`
reports the rank gain before you keep it.
- **Measured, not asser

ted.** A deterministic evaluation harness covers 12
scenario suites with hard functional gates and a

rters for DSH, pi, ZCode, Claude Code and Markdown trees
(plus a relaxed JSON/JSONL/stdin contract)

default to dry-run, back up the source,
[该节后续省略]
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A session looks like this:

1. **Session start / resume:** the adapter calls `ensureContext()`; core returns
a hot index (pinned

entries, high-value entries, recent entries, digest
lines) within a token budget. The adapter injec

ts it into the system prompt
once and keeps it byte-stable until it is invalidated.
2. **During the

session:** the model uses the memory tools (or the CLI) to
write, search, read, forget and inspect m

emories. Writes are deduplicated
and scoped; conflicting facts supersede old ones instead of overwri

ting
history.
3. **Session end:** the adapter sends a transcript digest to one bounded LLM
call, the

n writes the extracted memories (deduped against the existing
store, with a confidence threshold and

an idempotent cursor).
4. **Between sessions:** consolidation merges near-duplicates, retires stale
entries by value/age, and (optionally) writes topic digests.

## Security and privacy

HarnMem is local-first: no telemetry, no background service, and the engine never
opens a network co

nnection. The CLI is offline by default too; the only outbound
call is the opt-in `harnmem synonyms

suggest --llm-url` bridge, which runs solely
when you pass an endpoint. Memory content is sensitive

by nature — back up
`~/.harnmem/`, keep it out of version control, and read
SECURITY.md before repor

ting a vulnerability. The store uses
symlink/path containment checks, size caps, sensitive-value red

action, soft
delete and an audit log; see the design docs for details.
